P-01.headline: Two baskets, two windows, one finish time
P-01.best_for: Cooked-for-two households that want a main and a side done at once
P-01.tradeoff: Two small baskets instead of one big one; 450 °F max, and the listing's own capacity field says 6 liters
faq: What is the total capacity?
6 quarts, split into two independent 3-quart baskets, according to the listing title and bullets. The product-details Measurements field says 6 liters, which is about 6.3 quarts. Flagged as FLG-034.
Does it have a preheat function?
The listing does not state a preheat step. Presets and a +2 minute button are listed. Do not assume preheat.
What is the maximum temperature?
450 °F, per the listing's About this item bullets and Max Temperature Setting field.
Is it dishwasher safe?
The listing says the removable non-stick coated baskets are dishwasher safe.

qa: Do you cook a main and a side at the same time?
If you cook one thing at a time, two 3-quart baskets buy you nothing over one 8-quart basket.
Will 11.81 in of width plus clearance fit your counter?
Measured width is 11.81 in, depth 13.38 in, and weight 13.3 pounds. Add rear and above clearance for the vents.
Do you want to watch the food cook?
The windows are the differentiator here versus the 8-quart Chefman. Worth checking you would actually use them.

P-02.headline: A countertop oven that happens to air-fry
P-02.best_for: Households of 4–6 that want one appliance to roast, toast, air-fry and rotisserie
P-02.tradeoff: 16.9 in of depth plus French-door swing, item weight unstated on listing (FLG-022), and the listing contradicts itself on preset count and accessory count
faq: How many presets does it have?

The listing is inconsistent: the title, Configuration and Product Description say 24 one-touch presets, while the About this item bullet says 25 cooking pre-sets. Both are published here and neither is chosen. Flagged as FLG-021.
How many accessories are included?

The title says six cooking accessories, the Configuration field and Product Description say 7 accessories, and Included Components names six: rack, bake pan, drip tray, crisper basket, rotisserie spit, fetch tool. Flagged as FLG-031.
Will a 12-inch pizza fit?
The listing's own About this item bullet says it can bake a 12-inch pizza and rotisserie a 6-lb chicken.
Does it air-fry or is it just a toaster oven?
The listing has an Air Frying Technology field set to True and describes 360° superheated hot air circulation up to 500 °F at 1700 watts. It air-fries using oven-style circulation, not a basket.

qa: Do you have 16.9 in of depth, plus room for French doors to swing?
Depth is the binding constraint on most counters. Doors pull open in front of the unit.
Will you actually rotisserie?
The spit and fetch tool are part of what you pay for. Unused accessories are still footprint.
Are you willing to leave it in one place?
At 16.9 in deep and 15.8 in wide (with item weight unstated on the listing, FLG-022), this is a park-it-and-keep-it appliance, not something you lift into a cupboard.
Do you need a preset count you can rely on?
The listing says 24 in one place and 25 in another. If a specific preset matters to you, check the current listing before buying.

P-03.headline: One basket, no windows, four buttons
P-03.best_for: Households cooking one thing at a time who want maximum basket for the footprint
P-03.tradeoff: No window, single zone, and the listing contradicts itself on top temperature and wattage
faq: What is the maximum temperature?

Conflicting: the About this item bullet and Max Temperature Setting spec field say 400 °F, while the listing title advertises a 450 °F Hi-Fry option. Both are published; neither is chosen. Flagged as FLG-018.
How many watts?
Conflicting: the Features & Specs Output Wattage and Wattage fields say 1700 watts, while the About this item bullet says 1000 watts / 120 volts. Both are shown here and flagged as FLG-017.
Is the basket dishwasher safe?
Yes, the listing says the non-stick basket and flat frying tray are both top-rack dishwasher safe.
Does it come with a warranty?
The listing's warranty field says 1-Year Limited Warranty provided by Chefman.

qa: One basket or two — which matches your weeknight?
One 8-quart basket (12.8 lb unit) beats two 3-quart baskets if you cook in batches rather than in parallel.
Is 400 °F top temperature enough?
The spec field says 400 °F. The title advertises a 450 °F Hi-Fry option. That gap is flagged as FLG-018; check the manual if high-heat crisping matters.
Do you need to see the food?
There is no window on this model. You rely on the LED shake reminder and the timer.

P-04.headline: The one you keep in a drawer and grab
P-04.best_for: Grill and oven cooks who check temperature at the appliance and want zero setup
P-04.tradeoff: Accuracy and certification are seller claims, not independent test results; no walk-away monitoring
faq: How fast is it?
The listing states a 1 second response time using a thermocouple sensor (model HT07).
Is the NIST and NSF certification verified?

The listing states NIST and NSF under Specification Met and ships a calibration certificate. This site has not seen the certificate or an independent test report, so treat it as a seller claim (FLG-035).
What is the highest temperature it reads?
572 °F, per the Upper Temperature Rating field in Product information.
Can I put it in the dishwasher?
The listing's care instruction is Wipe Clean. Do not assume dishwasher safe.

qa: Do you check at the grill, or do you want to walk away?
This is a hand-held instant-read with a 6.5-inch length/immersion spec. If you want to leave the room, you want P-05 instead.
Do you need a certificate, or is a claim enough?
The listing includes a calibration certificate in the box. NIST and NSF are listed as specifications met — that is a seller statement, not a test report you can read here (FLG-035).
Will you wipe it rather than wash it?
The listing's care instruction is Wipe Clean, even though the title says IP67 waterproof.

P-05.headline: Three probes, no standing at the grill
P-05.best_for: Smoker and multi-protein cooks who want to monitor from inside the house
P-05.tradeoff: The listing contradicts itself on battery life and warranty length, and it depends on an app plus WiFi
faq: How long does the battery last?

The About this item bullet says up to 50 hours on a full charge. An earlier capture recorded 70 hours from Product Description text not visible in current fetched HTML. Both are flagged; treat 50 hours as the current listing claim. See FLG-008.
How many probes come in the box?
Three 4.75-inch probes, plus the hub (model CQ60-3C-Z1-E). Note the listing also sells 1, 2 and 4 probe options — check the size selector before buying.
Does it work without WiFi?
The listing says Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Bluetooth pairing is described in the bullets, but the marketing is built around Wi-Fi unlimited range. Do not assume full range without Wi-Fi.
Is it dishwasher safe, and what is the warranty?

The listing says the probes are waterproof and dishwasher safe (hub care is unstated). On warranty, About this item states a two-year assurance while Item details Warranty Description says 3 Year (FLG-019).

qa: Do you cook several proteins at once?
Three probes only pay off if you actually use more than one at a time.
Are you fine relying on an app and WiFi for doneness?
Remote monitoring is the product. If the app or network is a problem for you, P-04 is the safer buy.
Will you charge and clean three probes after every cook?
The hub charges all three at once, but they still need washing. The listing says the probes are dishwasher safe.
Do you need a warranty figure you can rely on?
The listing states two-year assurance in About this item and 3 Year in Item details (while an earlier register said 1-year). Flagged as FLG-019; confirm before relying on it.
